correctness.rationale: Every projected pairwise-vertex squared distance equals the original edge length squared minus the squared normal component. Exhausting all six edge vectors gives the exact adjacent-order-gap formula. The maximum gap follows from a sharp sum-of-squares inequality, and the normal distribution follows from a 48-fold signed-permutation spherical chamber with an exact projective Jacobian and two explicit active-bound branches. The upper-endpoint coefficient is the chamber-wall tube constant; the lower coefficient follows from a transverse two-dimensional tangent cone and a computed Jacobian. The executable independently enumerated projected edges on 90,000 random normals, compared the exact quadrature against 900,000 simulated normals, and confirmed both constants by decreasing-scale numerical integration. The proof, not the finite experiments, establishes the continuum claim.

originality.rationale: The claimed object is the diameter of a two-dimensional orthogonal shadow, which equals the centered projected circumradius of the tetrahedral difference body; this dual formulation was explicitly searched. Finch (2012) computes tetrahedral shadow area and perimeter, Henk–Böröczky (1997/2000) compute projected face-count asymptotics, and the closest other studies treat octahedral section diameters or octahedral projection inradii. None of the inspected relevant primary material or returned claim summaries states the adjacent-gap law, its one-dimensional CDF quadrature, the twelve minimizing planes, and both sharp endpoint coefficients. Scientific priority remains provisional because no literature search can establish global uniqueness.

value.rationale: Maximum Feret diameter is a canonical and practically interpretable planar-shadow metric; unlike area and perimeter, it is a maximum of all projected edge lengths. The exact CDF turns the natural regular tetrahedron into a fully calibrated example, and the minimizing twelve view planes solve a sharp nontrivial orientation problem. The unequal quadratic and square-root endpoint exponents identify distinct local geometric mechanisms, not arbitrary parameter refinements or a trivial normalization check. The result is mathematically self-contained and reproducible, even without a downstream application theorem.
risks: No extension to arbitrary simplices is established.
Historical overlap may reduce the scientific increment if an earlier full projected-cuboctahedron radial distribution is found.
